data.creator_notes:
There are, generally speaking, four reasons that NTR bots are NTR bots, or there is some combination of these four factors.
1. {{user}} is or was, at some point, a prick.
2. {{char}} is a complete sociopath.
3. Blackmail
4. {{char}} is afraid to talk about their feelings.
The first one is speaking for {{user}}, and that's dumb. There are tragedy of error scenarios in which it convincingly LOOKS like {{user}} did something they didn't do, and that's more compelling, but still, maybe talk about that shit. In the second, usually, {{char}} just completely heel-turns at the drop of a hat, or was always cartoonishly cruel and manipulative. You have lost nothing save the time and energy expended in being with that person for their moving on. Three sucks, but again, you talk about that shit with your partner and try and find a solution, or at the very least, you don't become enamored with or addicted to banging the person doing the blackmailing, as coercion is, for most of us, a bit of a turn-off.
That leaves number four. This can be the result of good intentions or fear I guess - not wanting to hurt your partner's feelings, or because you are ashamed of some hidden desire and just really don't want your partner to think less of you. That makes for fine drama, but if you're in a committed relationship and you aren't a goddamn child, you take a step back and ask, "Is setting the plane on fire really going to solve the engine trouble?"
Folks, I'm'a be real for all you whippersnappers who's concept of relationships has been colored by porn tropes - if they're cheating on you, unless they have at least one severe and untreated personality disorder, it's because communication has systemically failed at multiple levels in the relationship. That could be their fault or could be yours, but the answer usually lies somewhere between. Sociopaths are real, don't get me wrong, but that is the minority of cases.
On the other side of things, anti-NTR has this tendency to make characters that act kind of brainwashed - like, you could be a complete asshole to them and they'll still blindly love you forever. That isn't really very real either. The fact is that most people are loyal to their partners, but there is a limit if said partner won't do anything to earn it. So, here we are.
I have labeled this bot with both possible NTR and anti-NTR, because in most of the scenarios, Marlene needs something she's not getting, or has been introduced to something she has feelings about, and is coming to you, the partner whom she loves, to deal with it. If you completely refuse to acknowledge her concerns, then yeah, she might just cheat, but will probably just dump your ass. If that happens though, it's kind of on you.
I tried to include openers that represented dealing with the more common NTR tropes, and ways one might deal with those temptations in a better way than running off and hopping on somebody else. I have included links below to some mini-bots made for group chat for characters pertinent to some of the openers, most of which I suspect you won't even deal with directly anyway, so they are really more for completeness's sake. Actually dealing with Jenny and Bill, for an example, is something you have to kind of work to make happen. I tried to make the mini-bots defy stereotypes too, at least a little bit. Any other openings you would like to see, or if you think I missed something, hit me up. As a final note, because like 75% of NTR seems like it focuses on dick size, that theme is significantly represented. I made sure it wasn't the single metric by which everybody decides the quality of sexual experience, though.
